seven_q.Q0_posture: Analytical and constructive — the document assumes that structural parallels between ecology and ecclesiology are real and informative, not merely metaphorical
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record (ISO-028) establishing a structural mapping between ecological community dynamics and Pauline ecclesiology
seven_q.Q2_domain: Biology (ecology) and Christian theology (ecclesiology), with mathematics (diversity indices, power laws) as a bridging language
seven_q.Q3_claim: The structural dynamics of diverse, interdependent communities are isomorphic between ecosystems and churches — biodiversity maps onto gift diversity, keystone species onto apostolic/pastoral roles, trophic cascades onto leadership failure propagation, invasive species onto heresy, ecological succession onto church maturation, carrying capacity onto community size limits, mutualism/parasitism onto ministry partnerships/exploitative leadership, nutrient cycling onto teaching/discipleship cycles, edge effects onto missional boundary, and resilience onto spiritual health
seven_q.Q4_support: Ten specific correspondences with mathematical formulations (Shannon diversity index, species-area power law), empirical evidence from ecology (Yellowstone wolf removal, invasive species data, species-area relationship), scriptural evidence (1 Cor 12, Eph 4, Ezek 34, Gal 1, Acts 2, Heb 5, 3 John, Rom 12), swap test (passed — specific to ecology, not generic systems science), bidirectional predictions, and five falsification conditions
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Depends on the reality of structural isomorphisms between domains (ISO methodology), the validity of ecological principles (diversity-resilience, keystone species, trophic cascades, succession, species-area relationship, carrying capacity, edge effects), and the Pauline body metaphor as a structurally accurate description of church function
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Forces that church models suppressing gift diversity are structurally fragile; that leadership concentration without distribution is catastrophic upon leader removal; that heresy has an invasive advantage requiring active removal; that church planting follows predictable maturation stages; that optimal church size exists for relational health; that the most vigorous growth occurs at the church-culture boundary; that ecology gives ecclesiology a structural reason for gift diversity beyond politeness
seven_q.Q7_kill: Show that monoculture ecosystems/churches are equally or more resilient than diverse ones (break diversity-resilience); show that keystone species/leader removal has only localized effects (break cascade structure); show that church development does not follow a predictable maturation sequence (break succession); show that community size has no structural consequences for relational function (break carrying capacity); show that heretical movements do not outcompete orthodox teaching in the short term (break invasive species parallel)
